subject: Competitive tradeoffs and POC acceptance criteria
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Evan Torres <evan.torres@finnect.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 08 Dec 2026 15:02:00 -0500
Subject: Competitive tradeoffs and POC acceptance criteria

Hi Evan — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap so we have alignment before we formalize the POC: 

High-level pain & goals (your wording):
- Current inference costs are spiking with bursty traffic; finance needs predictable unit economics.
- Latency-sensitive paths (clinical triage) cannot tolerate >120ms p99 for short prompts.
- Regulatory: patient PHI must remain in our VPC for certain use cases; on-prem option may be required later.

Decision criteria you prioritized (ranked by Finnect):
1) Latency at p99 (short prompts) — hard requirement
2) Cost per 1k tokens at our expected scale — target < $0.35/token equivalent
3) Data isolation / VPC/on-prem capability
4) Integration effort (SDKs, telemetry hooks)
5) Model quality for medical summarization (ROUGE / small eval set)

Proposed POC scope & acceptance criteria (attached workbook has test cases):
- Run a 2-week POC with a dedicated small pool (4 GPUs equivalent) and three test buckets: latency smoke, cost stress, and quality eval.
- Acceptance: latency p99 <= 120ms for 0.5–2.5k token requests on the latency bucket; median cost within 10% of projections in cost stress run; quality score >= baseline on 3 prioritized prompts.
- Fallback test: failover to a CPU-quantized variant must complete within 300ms with no data leakage.

Open questions for your team:
- Do you want us to run the POC against real PHI in your VPC or synthetic data? (Legal prefers synthetic to start)
- Which internal owner should sign the MSA addendum for VPC onboarding?
- Are there any special compliance artifacts Finnect needs pulled into the audit log during the POC?

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm synthetic vs real PHI for week 1 (reply by EOD Thu 12/10).
2) We share a final POC-Test-Plan.xlsx with measurable tests (attached) and a proposed start date of Mon 12/14.
3) Kickoff call to review runbook and role matrix — 30m the week of 12/14.

Attachments: POC-Test-Plan.xlsx, decision_criteria_matrix.pdf, finnect-demo-recording.mp4 (processing)

Thanks — I pulled Camila and Marissa in to make sure our runbook covers the technical smoke tests and contract/discount items.

—

From: Evan Torres <evan.torres@finnect.com>

Date: Tue, 08 Dec 2026 16:28:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Competitive tradeoffs and POC acceptance criteria

Naomi — appreciate the crisp recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Synthetic data for week 1 is preferred; we'll provide a sanitized dataset that mirrors distribution. Legal will want to sign off but this keeps the initial run fast.
- MSA addendum: please route to Priya Shah (procurement) priya.shah@finnect.com — cc'd via calendar invite once you send the DocuSign.
- Audit logs: we need request-level tracing with masked PHI in logs and a retention window of 90 days for the POC.

Two tradeoffs we discussed and want explicitly called out in the POC:
1) Putting caching on vs off — caching will reduce cost but may mask model regressions. Please include a manual toggle and one test with cache disabled.
2) Quantized model variant — acceptable for cost tests, but we want final-quality checks run on the full-precision variant.

We can do the kickoff on Tue 12/15 at 10am ET if that works for the team.

—
Evan Torres
VP Product, Finnect Health
evant@finnect.com | +1 (617) 555-0124

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 09 Dec 2026 09:05:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Competitive tradeoffs and POC acceptance criteria

Thanks Evan — noted on synthetic data + audit retention window. Naomi, two technical clarifications from my side: 

- Latency baseline: can you quantify whether the 120ms p99 expectation is for cold-start or warm-run? For our routing/runtime, warm-run is realistic; we'll design the latency bucket to include cold and warm sequences.
- For the cache-off test: we'll implement a tag in the request header to bypass prefix caching. I suggest we run the cache-off tests under a 24-hour traffic window with identical prompt mixes so we can compare quality and cost.

Competitive context: Finnect asked during the call how Redwood compares to Vendor X on two points — multi-model routing and audit telemetry. Short note: Vendor X has lower BOM cost at high volumes but limited VPC tooling and fewer fine-grained traces. We'll include a short appendix in the POC workbook that runs the same sample prompts against Vendor X (when they provide test creds) so you can see apples-to-apples metrics.

I'll add the latency test definitions and cache toggle steps to the POC-Test-Plan.xlsx and re-share by EOD. Naomi — can you confirm the kickoff time (Evan suggested 12/15 at 10am ET)?

—
Camila Reyes
